title: Nature Table
strapline: A low table by the window where the treasures of every walk are laid out, added to and pored over all year round.
intent: A nature table is the setting's living record of the outdoors — a place where the pinecone, the feather and the conker from today's walk are honoured, studied and returned to.
Bringing back, arranging and revisiting natural treasures grows careful looking, sorting and comparing — the roots of classifying and mathematics.
The table changes with the seasons — blossom in spring, seed heads in autumn, bare twigs in winter — making the turning year visible and expected.
Handling delicate natural objects and setting them out with care develops fine-motor control and a sense of value and respect for the living world.
It is a magnet for talk: children show, name, describe and wonder about what they and their friends have found.
Real knowledge and vocabulary settle in over time — the names of trees, seeds, shells and stones, and the words to describe them.
implementation: Set a low, well-lit table with magnifiers, sorting trays, small pots and a few good reference books, and let it grow from what children bring back.
Make adding to it a habit: after every walk or garden session, choose treasures to display and talk about where they came from.
Model the wondering: 'Where do you think this seed came from? Shall we look it up? Which tree has leaves like this one?'
Support sorting and comparing — group the smooth and the prickly, the biggest to the smallest, this season's finds and last season's.
Refresh with the seasons and photograph the table each month, so children can look back and see how the year has turned.
Invite families in — a note home asking for treasures from a weekend walk keeps the table living and links home and setting.
key_questions: Where do you think this seed came from? Which tree has leaves like this?
Can you group the smooth ones and the prickly ones?
Which is the biggest, and which is the smallest?
What's changed on the table since last season?
What did you find on your walk to bring back?
